title: Direct Preference Optimization from ratios to gradients
outcome: Derive the DPO loss from a regularized preference model and distinguish sequence log probabilities, temperature effects and held-out evaluation.

exercises.title: Evaluate the reference
exercises.task: Set policy and reference log odds equal for any positive beta.
exercises.expected: The loss for a positive preference is log 2.
exercises.answer: The initial classifier is indifferent under the pairwise parameterization.

exercises.title: Differentiate the two-action loss
exercises.task: Use beta 2 and zero reference-relative log-odds shift.
exercises.answer: The result includes the beta scale and the logistic residual; it should agree with finite differences.

exercises.title: Compare beta optima
exercises.task: Fit a3:1 preference ratio with beta 0.5,1 and 2 under a uniform reference.
exercises.hint: The optimum policy-logit shift is log 3 divided by beta.
exercises.answer: Initial gradient magnitude and final optimum displacement are different properties of the objective.

exercises.title: Change length normalization
exercises.task: Use the token log-ratio arrays in the reference exercise.
exercises.expected: The sequence-sum margin is negative while the mean-token margin is positive.
exercises.hint: Chosen and rejected sequences have different lengths.
exercises.answer: Normalizing each sequence by its own length changes its relative contribution and therefore the objective.

exercises.title: Protect the reference
exercises.task: Update the reference parameters while retaining the same loss label.
exercises.hint: The reference is part of the training specification.
exercises.answer: Reference refresh can be a deliberate algorithmic choice, but it is not the same fixed-reference DPO problem.

exercises.title: Bound the claim
exercises.task: Observe a lower training DPO loss.
exercises.expected: Conclude improved fit to the declared preference objective only.
exercises.hint: Separate training labels from independent task outcomes.
exercises.answer: Task utility, robustness, calibration and critical constraints still need their own held-out evaluation.
